terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: The admitted GG DryStoneWall_Straight evidence is authoritative for the four-course rhythm, staggered rounded blocks, irregular silhouette, and roughly 1.0:0.89 run-to-height proportion. Suma authors that rhythm as two independent two-course half-tile modules so players can build at half-tile increments; two stacked modules reproduce the observed four-course read.

reasoning: The audited GG DryStoneWall_Straight mesh reads as four staggered courses of rounded irregular masonry.

A 0.675 m authored support interval becomes exactly half a tile; two stacked modules form the observed four-course, one-tile wall. The ordinary 1.43 m masonry face adds 0.059 live units of controlled straight-run overlap.
Cell-centred perpendicular walls require a conditional 2.15 m recessed junction span to reach the neighbouring wall face without enlarging isolated modules.
A recessed solid core is an implementation inference required to prevent through-gaps between rounded procedural stones.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate depth captures repeated stone courses and strict grid fit without inventing unseen geometry.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Irregular rounded stone outlines remain intact.
Each half-tile module has two horizontal courses; two stacked modules reproduce four readable courses.
Top stones retain a lightly irregular silhouette.
Ordinary endpoint stones overlap straight neighbours; conditional recessed arms close perpendicular corner and T-junction gaps.
Warm stone values vary between blocks without texture stretching.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

Raised or recessed relief and fasteners must be geometry, instanced micro-parts, or displacement; a map alone is an approximation (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: One-tile wall envelope and overlap contract
Warm stone variation and recessed cavity response

sculptPipeline.blockedReason: blockout requires a Godot capture and self-correction review before structural-pass unlocks
nextRequiredEvidence: blockout Godot render from the generated review project
AI vision score >= 0.7 with layer scores and mismatch critique
critical semantic feature scores from the same image pair meeting their individual thresholds
reviewHistory entry for blockout with action=continue

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: The audited stylized mesh proves shape and course layout; its export has no usable authored material, so Suma uses independent palette materials rather than inferred photographic PBR maps.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Node3D pivot with a MeshInstance3D child, action metadata, optional Marker3D sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: One tile is 1.0 runtime world unit and ordinary structure visuals receive the configured 0.74074074 scale.
The model's source Y axis is its masonry run and is rotated onto game-local X before export.
A roughly half-tile live depth is acceptable for a substantial dry-stone house wall.

coordinateFrame.front: negative local Z after Godot imports Blender's Z-up GLB as Y-up
coordinateFrame.up: positive local Z in Blender and positive local Y in Godot
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: authored 1.43 m face width, conditional 2.15 m junction span, and 0.675 m height; runtime scale yields a 1.059-unit straight-run face, a 1.593-unit perpendicular join span, and exactly 0.5-unit height

silhouette.boundingShape: near-square wall elevation with a shallow rectangular footprint and lightly uneven stone perimeter
silhouette.symmetry: approximately bilateral at module scale, intentionally asymmetric at individual stones
negativeSpaces: narrow recessed joints between stones; no through-gaps

observations: The admitted GG DryStoneWall_Straight evidence shows rounded warm-white rocks in four staggered courses.
The audited straight mesh spans approximately one grid interval along its run and uses a shallow wall depth.
Suma's cell-centred topology additionally requires hidden conditional endpoint closure where perpendicular walls occupy neighbouring cells.

componentTree.name: Modular Polished Stone Wall
componentTree.topologyRationale: The admitted GG evidence is an assembled dry-stone module; Suma recreates that observed assembly with procedural rounded slabs around a recessed gap-proof core.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: generate a deterministic gap-proof masonry module from reusable rounded-slab primitives
deformationStack: two staggered procedural courses per half-tile module
bounded 1.43 m seam-safe face around a 0.675 m support interval
slight per-stone width, height, and roll variation
geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: no stretched image textures; palette materials and analytic primitive normals
geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: analytic rounded-slab normals with closed flat front and back caps

dimensions.units: meters authored before runtime structure scale

collider.notes: Replace with sphere/capsule/compound proxy when the object shape demands it.

localFeatures.description: Give every visible stone a rounded rectangular perimeter with bounded asymmetry.
Preserve two distinct courses per module so two stacked modules reproduce the admitted four-course GG rhythm.
Preserve staggered recessed seams and avoid any new through-gaps.
Ordinary face bounds terminate at -0.715 and +0.715 m for straight overlap; topology-aware recessed arms reach -1.075 or +1.075 m only when a perpendicular neighbour needs closure.
Bounded stone height variation gives a lightly irregular top line while the support interval remains exact.
Alternate restrained warm stone palette values per block.

surfaceDetail.notes: Stone edges are real rounded geometry; every slab has a closed full-perimeter planar rear face with valid outward normals and no inset lip. A recessed core and cavity-toned material preserve readable joints without any through-holes.

componentTree.name: Recessed structural core
componentTree.topologyRationale: Rounded blocks visibly leave deep joints; an inset opaque core is the minimal inferred geometry that prevents those joints becoming holes.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: opaque infill behind every course, recessed from all visible masonry planes to avoid coplanar side artifacts

localFeatures.description: Core remains recessed behind block faces but spans every module seam.

componentTree.name: Conditional recessed junction arms
componentTree.topologyRationale: This is a Suma grid-fit inference: a neighbouring perpendicular wall sits beyond the ordinary endpoint, so only the facing end reveals a recessed core-and-course extension.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: two short recessed course stones around an opaque core extension
deformationStack: visibility selected from wall-neighbour rotation parity

localFeatures.description: The facing arm reaches the perpendicular wall face with a small hidden overlap; the open arm remains invisible.

componentTree.name: Lower masonry course
componentTree.topologyRationale: The admitted module shows a grounded row of broad rounded stones with recessed joints.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: three to four overlapping rounded slabs

localFeatures.description: Lowest blocks overlap the seating plane slightly and have no floating gap.

componentTree.name: Upper staggered course
componentTree.topologyRationale: Alternating joint positions between the lower and upper rows are the wall's main dry-stone identity cue.

localFeatures.description: Upper-course joints are offset from the lower row; stacked modules repeat the alternating two-course rhythm.

componentTree.name: Stacked-pair cap read
componentTree.topologyRationale: The cap read is supplied by the upper course of the second module in a stacked pair rather than a third course inside each half-tile module.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: derived from the upper course of a stacked module pair

localFeatures.description: Cap stones vary slightly but overlap the next stacked module's lower course.

materials.name: Base material

albedo.samplingNotes: Use image-observed local color zones, not a single averaged color.

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: Preserve stable world/object-scale detail; do not stretch micro detail with component scale.

surfaceFrequencyBands.role: ridges, pores, grain, dents, or equivalent visible relief
highlight breakup visible under grazing light

roughness.localResponse: crisp restrained rough-stone response under neutral and warm point lights; the sealed planar rear face has no protruding shoulder geometry

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darken creases, seams, intersections, and recessed local features.

shaderNotes: Use a Godot spatial ShaderMaterial when clearcoat, sheen, transmission, or thin-surface response is observed; otherwise use StandardMaterial3D-compatible PBR channels.
Generate albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO independently; never alias albedo into roughness.
Use normal/bump/displacement only when they map to observed surface relief.
Use displacement geometry when the observed relief changes the close-up silhouette; texture-only relief is insufficient there.
materials.notes: Warm matte palette values vary per procedural block; form detail comes from geometry rather than stretched textures.

materials.name: Recessed cavity core

albedo.samplingNotes: Inferred dark cavity value; not copied from the source asset.

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: No image texture; solid matte infill remains behind stones.

ambientOcclusion.notes: Recession and real-time contact shadows make the joints readable.

shaderNotes: Opaque by contract so no masonry joint can become a through-hole.
materials.notes: Implementation inference used only behind the observed stone courses.

acceptance: Silhouette reads correctly without materials.
Quality contract has named all required macro feature groups before code generation.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

visualEvidence.notes: Single-module review matches the four-course GG construction while retaining Suma's warmer palette and deterministic grid envelope.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The main silhouette, staggered courses, rounded blocks, and shallow wall depth are preserved. Suma remains slightly more regular and darker than the audited GG mesh; this is within the selected stylized-realtime fidelity target. Separate assembly and stack captures prove the inferred joins.

visualEvidence.notes: Two perpendicular neighbouring modules reveal only their facing junction arms and meet the long wall without a void.
Three modules resolve at exact one-tile height intervals with course overlap covering the vertical support seam.

reviewHistory.summary: Runtime-independent procedural wall accepted for the requested assembly and stacking interaction.
mismatches: Suma's warm palette is darker than the neutral GG evidence
Suma's deterministic stone widths are slightly more regular than the audited source
specFixes: recorded conditional junction arms as an explicit grid-fit inference
codeFixes: made endpoint arms topology-aware so isolated and straight walls keep the clean module silhouette

visualEvidence.notes: Assembly and stack captures were reviewed alongside the single-module comparison.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The requested interaction behavior clears the 0.7 acceptance threshold; remaining differences are restrained stylization rather than topology defects.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Reach accepted visual fidelity first, then optimize without removing reference-critical geometry or surface layers.

lightingFromPhoto.keyLight: warm-white directional key from upper front-left at approximately 45 degrees
lightingFromPhoto.toneMapping: Godot filmic tone mapping with restrained contrast
lightingFromPhoto.contactShadow: enabled beneath lower stones and inside recessed joints

lightingFromPhoto.fillLight: cool-neutral low-intensity fill from camera-right preserves cavity contrast
lightingFromPhoto.groundShadow: soft shadow on the tile seating plane

lightingFromPhoto.rimLight: soft environment light separates the upper course from the warm neutral background
lightingFromPhoto.ambientOcclusion: screen-space AO reinforces real geometric joints without making them black

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Use independent palette albedo and roughness because the audited GLB evidence has no usable source material maps.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
